description: O-read-singleton: actual two-node bootstrap/election, old-value application, committed self-removal of node 1, partition, node 2 election and new-value application. Request a unique ReadIndex from removed node 1 and observe Ready plus drained result. StepDownOnRemoval=true is a permitted nonresponse control.

harness.description: Serialized RawNode driver, actual message producers, faithful no-crash MemoryStorage. A simple application records committed payloads only to establish later-write ordering, not to claim completed client read.
semantic_changes: No target changes or direct state mutation. Partition drops every peer message after completed self-removal.
ReadStates are observed only for the unique request context; final result is always emitted after drain, including no-response control.
The post-request delivered-message counter is measured at the actual Step boundary.

legality.derivation: The caller uses supported APIs and actual committed membership entries, persists every Ready before transport and applies entries before Advance. StepDownOnRemoval is explicitly optional; no read API restriction requiring this option or mandatory removal shutdown is stated in the captured caller contract. Peer isolation is a permitted network fault. The sole remaining voter campaigns legally after applying removal and commits locally. No random clocks, manufactured replies or concurrent caller operations enter the checked response interval.
legality.applicability: ReadOnlySafe, no crashes or lease reads, fresh context, two-node membership changes while both nodes initially available.
alternatives: The application may stop removed nodes or enable immediate step-down; the control exercises the latter protection.

grounding.derivation: Within zero post-request peer communication, the local singleton shortcut can only have an eligible quorum if the local node is the sole installed voter. The implication read_returned => local_singleton_support tests this necessary condition; a missing response is permitted. The earlier applied write provides actual history but the result does not claim a client endpoint.
grounding.applicability: Correlated new read on node 1 after self-removal, zero delivered peer messages until result.
alternatives: Enabled step-down may drop the request; that is an allowed control.
Application-index waiting may block a client read; it does not give this responder an eligible quorum.

observable_properties.description: A returned ReadState with no post-request network support requires the local singleton voter to be the responder. Nonresponse is permitted.

uncertainties: No completed stale client read is observed; caller application wait remains outside the checked component.
This checks necessary local support in a singleton configuration, not sufficiency of arbitrary read-index histories.
